<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919126_theRebbe_561" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919126_theRebbe_561__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that fear of G-d, unlike love, comes primarily through human effort, and therefore the request "Hashem our G-d be with us" emphasizes His assistance to our own work.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one may add,</t>
    <t s="1">that the reason the term "treasury" is said specifically regarding fear,</t>
    <t s="2">even though this matter</t>
    <t s="3">(that the Holy One, blessed be He, needs, so to speak, man)</t>
    <t s="4">applies to all mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="5">for in order for the fulfillment of mitzvos to be as required, it is through love of Hashem or through fear of Hashem13,</t>
    <t s="6">and among the distinctions between love and fear is14,</t>
    <t s="7">that love of Hashem comes through a revelation of light from above,</t>
    <t s="8">and fear of Hashem comes</t>
    <t s="9">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="10">through the work of man.</t>
    <t s="11">And analogous to fear of a human king,</t>
    <t s="12">that the reason the people of the country fear the king is because they accepted him to be king over them15,</t>
    <t s="13">for the acceptance of kingship is through the people,</t>
    <t s="14">"You shall surely set a king over you"16.</t>
    <t s="15">And based on this, one can explain the phrase "May Hashem our G-d be with us as He was with our forefathers,"</t>
    <t s="16">for in fear of Hashem</t>
    <t s="17">(which is the beginning of service and its essence and root17),</t>
    <t s="18">the main thing is the work of man,</t>
    <t s="19">and the revelation of light from above</t>
    <t s="20">(Hashem our G-d)</t>
    <t s="21">is only an assistance to man,</t>
    <t s="22">"with us."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that fear, being total self-nullification like that of a servant, must come specifically through man's own acceptance of servitude, not through an external revelation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">Now, the reason for this, that fear comes primarily through the work of man,</t>
    <t s="2">one may say,</t>
    <t s="3">is because fear is self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="4">And particularly the fear of a king,</t>
    <t s="5">"You shall surely set a king over you, so that his awe shall be upon you"18,</t>
    <t s="6">that the self-nullification of this fear is connected with the fact that he is a servant of the king</t>
    <t s="7">[for the nature of a servant is that the awe and fear of the master is upon him],</t>
    <t s="8">that the self-nullification of a servant is total self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="9">and therefore it comes specifically through man,</t>
    <t s="10">for the action that is done in man through a revelation of light from above is like something additional to him,</t>
    <t s="11">and therefore the change that occurs in him through this is only in his mental conception,</t>
    <t s="12">but not a change in the man himself,</t>
    <t s="13">and in order to come to total self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="14">the self-nullification of a servant</t>
    <t s="15">[for the difference between a free man and a servant is in the very essence of his existence],</t>
    <t s="16">it is through man himself accepting upon himself to be a servant of the king.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that self-sacrifice, being total nullification, also comes primarily from man himself, so the request "May Hashem our G-d be with us" was fitting for the Rebbe's talk about self-sacrifice.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And one may say that the same applies to self-sacrifice (mesiras nefesh),</t>
    <t s="1">for since self-sacrifice is total self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="2">and particularly when the self-sacrifice is for matters that according to law</t>
    <t s="3">(a command from above)</t>
    <t s="4">one is not obligated to give his life for them19,</t>
    <t s="5">therefore it is</t>
    <t s="6">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="7">not through a revelation of light from above, but through man giving his life.</t>
    <t s="8">And based on this, it will be understood even more that the request and prayer of the Baal HaGeulah</t>
    <t s="9">(in the sicha of 3 Tammuz)</t>
    <t s="10">was in the language of the verse "May Hashem our G-d be with us as He was with our forefathers,"</t>
    <t s="11">for he spoke then about the matter of the service of self-sacrifice,</t>
    <t s="12">and in this very matter, regarding many matters that according to law one is not obligated to give his life for, which come</t>
    <t s="13">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="14">from man himself,</t>
    <t s="15">and since in the service of self-sacrifice the main thing is the work of man,</t>
    <t s="16">and the revelation of light from above assists the work of man,</t>
    <t s="17">therefore he began his request and prayer</t>
    <t s="18">(in the language of the verse)</t>
    <t s="19">"May Hashem our G-d be with us."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
